name: Await inside try preserves catch and finally control state

input.source_text: mut order = []; module M { public async fun inner(g) -> Object { try { let v = await g; order.append(:body); v } catch e { order.append(:caught); e } finally { order.append(:cleanup) } } } let g = Gate.new(); let t = M.inner(g); let posted = Gate.complete(g, 7); let resumed = Host.run(t); [resumed, order]

applicability.reason: Supported, and a real defect was fixed to get here. The earlier reason said the evaluator reports try/catch/finally containing await as UnsupportedConstruct; re-probing shows that was a measurement error. A bare `await` does not drive the scheduler - C063 makes `Host.run` the driver - so the refusal came from awaiting a task still registered as suspended, with no try involved at all. Driving correctly then exposed the actual defect: `finally` ran on SUSPENSION as well as on the real exit, so cleanup executed twice, in order [cleanup, body, cleanup]. C013 makes a suspension a registered continuation rather than an exit, so the protected region has not been left and `finally` has not been reached; the `using` path already guarded this for the same reason. Cleanup now runs once, and resumption retains the catch context and pending control state C025 requires.
